metal_surface_input_groups.description: Exterior metal is component-based with four paintable items, each with different UOMs. Railings and gutters are LF-based; ornamental and misc items are EA-based. Engine divides quantity by rate to calculate hours. All protection inputs are LF or SF based.

task_production_rates.name: Mobilization and Staging
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Load truck with metal-specific equipment: wire brushes, grinders, solvent wipes, DTM primers, spray equipment, ladders, tarps. Stage at work area. ~45 min (0.75 hr) — midpoint of 0.5-1.0 hr range. Slightly longer than interior mobilization because exterior metal requires specialty prep tools (grinders, wire wheels, rust converters) not typical for standard painting.

defect_tolerance.all: All required tools and materials on site. Staging area established.

task_production_rates.name: Scaffold Setup Per Facade
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Erect scaffolding for elevated metal work (high gutters, second-story railings, ornamental iron above ladder reach). 120 min (2.0 hr) per facade — midpoint of 1.75-2.5 hr range. 2-person crew required for scaffold assembly safety. Only when access_method = scaffold. Per facade/elevation.

defect_tolerance.all: Scaffold level, plumb, and secure. All guardrails installed. Toe boards in place. OSHA-compliant.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Along Metal Work Zone
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along work perimeter where landscape is adjacent to metal elements. ~29 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade. Critical for spray operations — metal overspray is difficult to remove from plantings. LF-based. Identical rate to masonry and siding siblings.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft). Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete perimeter coverage secured at all edges. No gaps in protection.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Double-layer in high-value landscape areas. All edges secured.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Below Metal Elements
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on hardscape below metal elements (porch floors under railings, walkways under gutters). ~14 sec per SF. Metal prep debris (rust flakes, grinding dust) and solvent overspray are particularly damaging to hardscape. Identical rate to sibling specs.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of hardscape within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage double-layered. Canvas on crew paths. All edges taped.

task_production_rates.name: Siding Protection Adjacent to Metal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask and protect siding adjacent to metal elements being painted. ~21 sec per SF. Poly sheeting taped to siding edges. Critical where gutters meet fascia, railings meet walls. Slightly slower than flat hardscape protection due to vertical taping.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of siding within spray zone. Tape lines clean.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines at all transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Fresh tape. Clean lines. Double-poly in high-visibility areas.

task_production_rates.name: Masonry Protection Adjacent to Metal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask and protect masonry adjacent to metal elements. ~21 sec per SF. Poly sheeting taped at metal-to-masonry transitions. Porous masonry absorbs metal primer overspray permanently if unprotected.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of masonry within spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines at all transitions.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. All porous surfaces double-masked.

task_production_rates.name: Light Fixture Masking Near Metal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape light fixtures adjacent to metal work with plastic and blue tape. ~7.5 min per fixture — midpoint of 5-10 min range. Slightly slower than siding spec (10 EA/hr) because metal-adjacent fixtures often require solvent-resistant masking (solvent wipe prep affects standard plastic).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All fixtures bagged. Complete coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All fixtures bagged with clean tape lines. Cover plates removed where accessible.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All fixtures bagged. Clean tape. Cover plates removed. Double-bag if spray operation.

task_production_rates.name: Roof Edge Protection Along Gutters
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply masking along roof edge above gutter line to protect roofing material from primer and paint overspray. ~29 sec per LF. Tape and poly along drip edge. Particularly important when spraying gutters — overspray drifts upward onto shingles.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Continuous masking along roof edge in spray zones.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete masking along all roof edges above painted gutters.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete masking. Double-width poly for wind protection.

task_production_rates.name: Metal Condition Assessment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual and tactile inspection of each metal component: identify substrate type (steel, aluminum, galvanized), existing coating condition, rust severity, corrosion patterns, loose/flaking paint, chalk, and structural integrity. ~7.5 min per component. Document findings per component. Gate task for prep selection.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Each component assessed. Substrate type identified. Condition documented.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Each component assessed with photo documentation. Substrate type confirmed. Detailed condition notes.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full assessment with photo documentation, substrate verification, coating thickness readings where applicable.

task_production_rates.name: Structural Rust / Integrity Check (Gate Task)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Inspect each component for structural rust (deep pitting, metal loss, compromised cross-section). ~7.5 min per component. Tap test, visual inspection of welds, check for through-rust. GATE TASK: structural rust = HARD STOP. Component requires welding/replacement before painting — outside painting scope. Document and flag for client.

defect_tolerance.all: Every component checked for structural integrity. Any structural rust documented and flagged to client before proceeding.

task_production_rates.name: SP1 Solvent Wipe Clean (Mandatory All Metal)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning — wipe ALL metal surfaces with solvent-dampened rags to remove oil, grease, dirt, fingerprints, and contaminants. 75 LF/hr midpoint of 50-100 range. ~48 sec per LF. MANDATORY first step for ALL metal substrates. If skipped, mechanical prep smears oils into surface causing adhesion failure. Clean rags only — contaminated rags re-deposit oils. For EA items, use 5 min/EA average.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All surfaces wiped clean. No visible oil, grease, or contaminants.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All surfaces wiped clean. White rag test passes (no transfer).
defect_tolerance.QT5: All surfaces wiped clean. White rag test documented. Two-pass wipe on critical areas.

task_production_rates.name: SP2 Hand Tool Prep (Wire Brush / Hand Sand)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: SSPC-SP 2 hand tool cleaning — wire brush, hand scraper, sandpaper to remove loose rust, loose paint, and mill scale. 30 LF/hr midpoint of 20-40 range. ~2 min per LF. Removes only loose material — does not remove tightly adhered rust or paint. Adequate for light surface rust on steel/iron where power tools are impractical (intricate profiles, tight spaces).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All loose rust and flaking paint removed. Surface free of loose material.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All loose material removed. Adjacent areas feathered smooth. No loose edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete removal of all loose material. Feathered edges. Profile verified by touch.

task_production_rates.name: SP3 Power Tool Prep (Grinder / Wire Wheel)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: SSPC-SP 3 power tool cleaning — angle grinder with wire wheel or flap disc to remove tight rust, mill scale, and failing paint down to bright metal. 18 LF/hr midpoint of 10-25 range. ~3.3 min per LF. Aggressive removal to near-white metal. Generates significant sparks and debris — requires eye protection, fire watch on dry days. Much slower than SP2 but dramatically better surface quality and coating longevity (4-5x longer life).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Tight rust and failing paint removed. Bright metal visible in treated areas.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete removal to bright metal. Uniform profile. No skip areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Near-white metal. Complete removal. Profile gauge verified. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Aluminum Surface Abrasion (Scotch-Brite / Fine Sand)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Abrade aluminum surfaces with Scotch-Brite pads or 180-grit sandpaper to create mechanical tooth for primer adhesion. 50 LF/hr midpoint of 40-60 range. ~1.2 min per LF. CRITICAL TIMING: primer must be applied within 15 minutes of abrading — aluminum re-forms Al2O3 oxide that resists adhesion. Work in small sections: abrade, prime immediately, move to next section.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform scuff pattern. No glossy untreated areas. Primed within 15 min.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete uniform abrasion. Dull matte finish. Primed within 15 min of each section.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete abrasion documented. Water-break test passes. Primed within 10 min.

task_production_rates.name: Galvanized Surface Cleaning (Vinegar / Ammonia Wash)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean galvanized surfaces to remove white rust, passivation oils, and zinc salts. 50 LF/hr midpoint of 40-60 range. ~1.2 min per LF. New galvanized steel has factory passivation oils that must be removed for primer adhesion. Vinegar wash (dilute acetic acid) or ammonia solution removes oils and lightly etches zinc surface. Rinse thoroughly after treatment.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Passivation oils removed. Water sheeting test passes.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete oil removal. Uniform water sheeting. No beading.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete cleaning documented. Water sheeting test passes everywhere. Photo documentation.

task_production_rates.name: Rust Conversion Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply phosphoric/tannic acid rust converter to transform iron oxide to stable ferric phosphate/tannate. 40 LF/hr midpoint of 30-50 range. ~1.5 min per LF. Includes: apply converter, wait 15-30 min for reaction, verify conversion (surface turns black), lightly abrade converted surface. Best for intricate profiles (scrollwork, balusters) where power tool access is impossible. Note: conversion only treats top layer — shorter coating life (1-3 yr) vs mechanical removal (4-5x longer). Tradeoff is labor efficiency on complex profiles.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Converter applied to all rusty areas. Surface turned black (confirmed conversion). Excess wiped.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete conversion. All areas verified. No active rust remaining. Lightly abraded.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete conversion documented. All areas verified and photographed. Abraded for primer adhesion.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Existing Coating
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scuff-sand or liquid degloss existing paint to create adhesion profile for new coating. 50 LF/hr midpoint of 40-60 range. ~1.2 min per LF. Only when existing paint is sound but glossy. If existing coating is failing, TSK_METL_STRIP_FAILING is used instead.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Existing gloss broken. Uniform dull surface. No glossy skip areas.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete degloss. Uniform matte appearance. Adhesion test passes.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete degloss documented. Cross-hatch adhesion test passes.

task_production_rates.name: Strip Failing Existing Coating
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove failing existing coating by chemical stripper, heat, or aggressive mechanical methods. 15 LF/hr midpoint of 10-20 range. ~4 min per LF. Most labor-intensive prep task. Used when existing coating is peeling, flaking, or delaminating extensively (>30% failure). After stripping, surface returns to bare metal state requiring full prime cycle.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All failing coating removed. Feathered edges at transition to sound coating.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete removal of all failing coating. Smooth transitions. No loose edges.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete removal to bare metal in all failed areas. Smooth feathered transitions documented.

task_production_rates.name: Post-Prep Dust and Debris Clean
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all grinding dust, wire brush debris, and rust particles from metal surfaces and surrounding areas after prep is complete. 100 LF/hr midpoint of 80-120 range. ~36 sec per LF. Compressed air blow-off, tack cloth wipe, and vacuum of drop cloths. Prep debris on metal causes inclusion defects under primer. Must be done between prep and prime phases.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Surface free of visible dust and debris. Drop cloths cleaned.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Surface tack-cloth clean. No visible particles. All debris collected.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Surface tack-cloth clean and verified. Compressed air verified. All debris collected and disposed.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Metal-to-Building Junctions
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply sealant at metal-to-building junctions (railing post bases, gutter end caps, downspout brackets, ornamental iron mounting points). 75 LF/hr midpoint of 50-100 range. ~48 sec per LF. Polyurethane or hybrid sealant — NOT silicone (silicone repels paint). Gun application + tool smooth. Prevents moisture intrusion behind metal elements which causes corrosion from the back side.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All metal-to-building junctions sealed. Clean bead. No gaps.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All junctions sealed. Tooled smooth. Consistent bead width. No voids.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All junctions sealed and tooled. Consistent profile. Documented. Backer rod where gaps >3/8 in.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — DTM Acrylic, Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply DTM acrylic primer to steel/iron surfaces. 20 LF/hr midpoint of 15-25 range. ~3 min per LF. Standard primer for ferrous metals. Brush application ensures primer is worked into all profiles, pits, and crevices. UV stable — tolerates longer recoat windows than epoxy. Water-based cleanup.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. No holidays or bare spots. Uniform film.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film build. All profiles coated. No runs or sags.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage verified. DFT spot-checked. All profiles coated. No defects.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — DTM Acrylic, Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray-apply DTM acrylic primer to steel/iron surfaces with back-brush follow on complex profiles. 32 LF/hr midpoint of 25-40 range per 2-person crew (sprayer + back-brusher). Spray provides faster coverage on long straight runs (gutters, straight railings). Back-brush ensures primer is worked into all profiles. 2-person crew rate.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Uniform film. Back-brushed on all profiles.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film build. All profiles back-brushed. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. DFT verified. All profiles back-brushed. No defects.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — DTM Alkyd, Brush Application (Pitted Surfaces)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply DTM alkyd primer to heavily pitted steel/iron. 20 LF/hr midpoint of 15-25 range. ~3 min per LF. Alkyd binder has superior wetting and flows into microscopic pits better than acrylic. BLOCKED on galvanized (saponification) and aluminum (insufficient flexibility). Solvent-based — mineral spirits cleanup. Brush-only for pit penetration.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Primer worked into all pits and crevices.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. All pits filled. Uniform film. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. DFT verified. All pits sealed. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — Etch Primer, Brush Application (Galvanized / Aluminum)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply etch (wash) primer to galvanized or aluminum surfaces. 25 LF/hr midpoint of 20-30 range. ~2.4 min per LF. Phosphoric acid in primer microscopically etches slick non-ferrous surfaces for adhesion. Thin film — do NOT over-apply. For aluminum: must apply within 15 minutes of surface abrading (Al2O3 reform window). Two-component product with limited pot life.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Thin uniform coat. No puddles or heavy areas. Complete coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Thin uniform coat. Complete coverage. Applied within prime window.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Thin uniform coat documented. Applied within prime window. DFT verified.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — Bonding Primer, Brush Application (Sound Existing Coating)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply bonding primer over sound existing coating after degloss. 25 LF/hr midpoint of 20-30 range. ~2.4 min per LF. Promotes adhesion between existing coating and new finish system. Used when existing coating is sound (no peeling/flaking) but requires new color or system change.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage over existing surface. Uniform film.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film. No bare spots. Cross-hatch adhesion passes.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. DFT verified. Adhesion test documented.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — Zinc-Rich Primer, Brush Application (QT5 Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply zinc-rich primer to carbon steel for cathodic (sacrificial) protection. 20 LF/hr midpoint of 15-25 range. ~3 min per LF. QT5 ONLY — requires near-white blast cleaning (SSPC-SP10) which exceeds QT3/QT4 scope. High zinc dust content (65-85% by weight in dry film). Very thick film. Heavy settling in can — constant stirring required. Specialty product. Must be topcoated — not UV stable.

defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Thick uniform film. DFT verified (3-4 mils). No holidays. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Prime — Surface-Tolerant Epoxy Primer, Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply two-component surface-tolerant epoxy primer on steel/iron where aggressive prep is impractical (intricate ornamental, occupied-adjacent). 20 LF/hr midpoint of 15-25 range. ~3 min per LF. Two-component mix — limited pot life (4-8 hrs). CRITICAL: must topcoat within recoat window (24-72 hrs) — epoxy chalks and loses adhesion if UV-exposed beyond window.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Mixed per manufacturer spec. Applied within pot life.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film. Topcoated within recoat window. Documented.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. DFT verified. Topcoated within window. All records documented.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Prime Bare Areas on Existing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot-prime bare metal areas exposed during prep (stripped spots, sanded-through areas, rust removal zones) on otherwise sound existing coating. 30 LF/hr midpoint of 20-40 range. ~2 min per LF. Faster than full prime because only treating discrete spots. Brush-only for precision on spot areas.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All bare spots primed. No exposed metal.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All bare spots primed. Feathered edges. Uniform film on spots.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All bare spots primed and documented. DFT verified on spot areas.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat — DTM Acrylic, Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply DTM acrylic finish coat to metal surfaces. 20 LF/hr midpoint of 15-25 range. ~3 min per LF. Brush application for railings, ornamental profiles, and areas where spray is impractical. Provides maximum control on complex profiles. Self-priming DTM acrylic — same product can serve as primer and finish in some systems. Per coat — multiply by coat count for total.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Uniform color and sheen. No holidays, runs, or sags.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film. Consistent sheen. No brush marks on flat sections.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Uniform film verified. Consistent color/sheen. No defects. DFT spot-checked.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat — DTM Acrylic, Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray-apply DTM acrylic finish coat to metal surfaces. 32 LF/hr midpoint of 25-40 range. Airless spray for long runs (gutters, straight railings). Faster than brush on simple profiles. Single operator for straight runs. Per coat — multiply by coat count for total.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. Uniform color and sheen. No runs, sags, or orange peel.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film. Even sheen. No overspray on adjacent surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. DFT verified. Uniform appearance. No defects. Film build documented.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat — DTM Acrylic, Spray + Back-Brush
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray-apply DTM acrylic finish coat with immediate back-brush by second crew member. 32 LF/hr midpoint of 25-40 range per 2-person crew. Sprayer applies material, back-brusher works it into profiles and eliminates runs/sags. Best method for complex profiles — combines spray speed with brush detail. 2-person crew rate. Per coat — multiply by coat count for total.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. All profiles back-brushed. Uniform appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. All profiles back-brushed. No runs. Uniform sheen.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. All profiles back-brushed. DFT verified. No defects. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Ornamental Detail Finish (EA Items)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Detailed brush finish on ornamental iron and miscellaneous discrete items. 3 EA/hr = ~20 min/EA midpoint of 15-30 min range. Covers ornamental iron pieces (finials, scrollwork, gate hardware) and misc items (mailbox posts, light poles). Artist-quality brush work on complex 3D profiles. Per coat — multiply by coat count for total.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage on all surfaces. No holidays. Uniform appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Uniform film on all profiles. No runs, sags, or missed areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Museum-quality coverage. All surfaces coated. Film verified. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Final Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of all coated metal surfaces for holidays, runs, sags, missed areas, and color/sheen consistency. 100 LF/hr midpoint of 80-120 range. ~36 sec per LF. Systematic walk-around at multiple distances. Mark defects for touchup.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Walk-around inspection. All visible defects marked.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic inspection at close range. All defects marked. Film build spot-checked.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Comprehensive inspection with documentation. DFT readings. Photo record. All defects marked.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of marked defects from inspection — holidays, light spots, runs (sand and recoat), drips, and missed areas. 30 LF/hr midpoint of 20-40 range. ~2 min per LF average. Rate reflects LF scanned for touch-up — most LF passes without repair. Actual defect repair is slower but defect density is low on properly applied work.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All marked defects corrected. Uniform appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects corrected. Touch-up blends with surrounding finish. No visible repair lines.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects corrected and verified. Touch-up invisible. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Protection Materials
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all tarps, plastic sheeting, tape, and masking from protected areas. 22 min (0.37 hr) — midpoint of 0.25-0.5 hr (15-30 min) range. Includes careful tape removal to avoid pulling fresh paint, folding/rolling protection materials, and spot-cleaning any overspray on protected surfaces.

defect_tolerance.all: All protection materials removed. No tape residue. No paint transfer to protected surfaces. Adjacent surfaces clean.

task_production_rates.name: Scaffold Teardown Per Facade
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Disassemble scaffolding per facade. 75 min (1.25 hr) — midpoint of 1.0-1.5 hr (60-90 min) range. 2-person crew. Faster than setup because no leveling required — just disassemble and stack. Per facade/elevation.

defect_tolerance.all: All scaffold components removed. No damage to building surfaces. Hardware collected.

task_production_rates.name: Final Site Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final cleanup: collect all debris (wire brush fragments, grinding dust, rust flakes, caulk tubes, solvent rags), clean equipment, dispose of hazardous waste (solvent rags, rust converter bottles) per local regulations, sweep work area. 22 min — midpoint of 0.25-0.5 hr (15-30 min) range. Metal prep generates more hazardous debris than standard painting — solvent-contaminated rags require fire-safe disposal.

defect_tolerance.all: Work area clean. All debris collected. Hazardous waste properly disposed. Equipment cleaned and stored.

factor_modifiers.name: Metal Profile Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Metal surface complexity is the primary labor driver. Standard (simple pickets, straight gutters) = 1.0x baseline. Moderate (multi-plane profiles, minor decorative elements) = 1.5x. Ornate (historic ironwork, scrollwork, intricate patterns) = 2.5x (midpoint of 2.0-3.0 research range). Complexity increases prep time (more surfaces to clean/sand), coating time (brush detail into crevices), and material consumption (more surface area per LF).
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied to ALL prep and coating tasks per the spec instruction. Protection and fixed tasks are NOT affected — protection scope is driven by area, not metal complexity. Standard = simple pickets, straight gutters/downspouts, flat panels. Moderate = multi-story railings, decorative cap rails, multi-plane gutter profiles. Ornate = historic scrollwork, hand-forged balusters, cast ornamental panels. WARNING: Ornate (2.50x) combined with scaffold access (1.60x) = 4.00x — at the stacking cap. See modifier_stacking_examples.

factor_modifiers.name: Exterior Access Method Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access method affects production rate for all tasks performed at elevation. Ground is baseline. Ladder adds repositioning time and single-hand work limitations. Scaffold provides stable platform but adds setup/teardown overhead (captured in separate fixed tasks). Lift provides stable elevated platform with good mobility.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Protection setup/teardown, mobilization, scaffold setup/teardown, and site cleanup are ground-level tasks — not affected. Scaffold access modifier covers the on-scaffold productivity penalty only — scaffold erection/teardown time is captured in separate FIXED tasks (TSK_METL_SCAFFOLD_SETUP, TSK_METL_SCAFFOLD_TEARDOWN). Ladder is most common for gutters and second-story railings. Scaffold for multi-story ornamental facades.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects overall production pace for binary tasks. QT3 is baseline. QT4 adds inspection detail and application thoroughness. QT5 adds documentation, DFT verification, and premium application techniques. No QT2 for exterior metal.
factor_modifiers.notes: No QT2 for exterior metal — minimum tier is QT3. QT4 adds 15% time for increased inspection detail, more thorough prep verification, and careful application. QT5 adds 30% for DFT verification, photo documentation, premium application techniques, and museum-quality finish expectations. Applied to all binary tasks. Fixed tasks (mobilize, scaffold, cleanup) are not quality-tier sensitive.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind affects spray operations (overspray drift, pattern disruption). High wind blocks spray entirely per SOP exclude_when. Moderate wind slows spray work.
factor_modifiers.notes: High wind BLOCKS spray operations per SOP site_condition_rules. Moderate wind (5-10 mph) slows spray 15% due to pattern disruption and repositioning. Brush operations are not significantly affected by wind — modifier applies to spray tasks only. Metal spray generates more overspray than flat surface spray due to profile deflection.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Direct sun on metal surfaces causes rapid heating — dark metal can exceed 140F in direct sun, causing flash drying of coatings, rapid solvent evaporation, and poor film formation.
factor_modifiers.notes: Metal heats faster and hotter than masonry or wood in direct sun. Full sun modifier is 1.20x (vs 1.15x for masonry) because metal's thermal conductivity causes more rapid surface temperature increase. Forces elevation sequencing (shaded elevations first) and may require early morning/late afternoon scheduling. Dark colors amplify the effect.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Extreme surface temperatures affect coating application. Cold surfaces (<50F) extend recoat intervals. Hot surfaces (>90F) cause flash drying — BLOCKED on metal because metal heats faster than other substrates.
factor_modifiers.notes: Optimal: 50-90F surface temp. Cold surface (<50F): coatings cure slower, recoat windows extend, productivity drops 10%. Hot surface (>90F): BLOCKED per SOP — coating flash-dries on contact with hot metal, causing poor film formation, blistering, and adhesion failure. Metal reaches BLOCKED temperature faster than wood or masonry due to high thermal conductivity.

quality_effects.notes: Standard tier. Single prime coat + single finish coat. Visual inspection. Adequate corrosion protection for typical residential metal elements with standard maintenance cycle (5-7 year recoat). SP1 solvent clean mandatory. SP2/SP3 as needed by condition.

Premium tier. Single prime coat + two finish coats. Interstage inspection between finish coats. Systematic inspection with DFT spot-checks. Enhanced corrosion protection (7-10 year recoat cycle). More thorough prep per QT modifier.

Archival tier. Single prime coat (zinc-rich on critical steel) + two finish coats. Interstage sand between finish coats for intercoat adhesion. Comprehensive inspection with DFT readings, photo documentation, and adhesion testing. Maximum corrosion protection (10-15 year recoat cycle). Near-white prep standard. Specialty primers available.

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backbrush are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + back-brusher). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for spray (no back-brush) and brush are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
All LF rates are calibrated to standard-profile metal (simple pickets, straight gutters). Profile complexity modifier adjusts for moderate and ornate profiles.
SP1 solvent clean is ALWAYS required — it is a binary task with no conditional gate. Skipping SP1 is the #1 cause of metal coating failure.
Structural rust is a HARD STOP — component must be repaired/replaced before painting. TSK_METL_STRUCTURAL_RUST_CHECK is a gate task.
Galvanized steel: oil/alkyd primers are BLOCKED (saponification). Only acrylic DTM, etch, or epoxy primers allowed.
Aluminum: primer must be applied within 15 minutes of surface abrasion (Al2O3 reform window). Work in small sections.
Rust conversion is a labor/life-expectancy tradeoff: faster than mechanical removal but 1-3 year coating life vs 4-5x longer for mechanical prep. Choice driven by profile complexity and access.
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (profile_complexity x access x QT).
Maximum combined modifier: 5.20x (ornate + scaffold + QT5) — EXCEEDS 4.0x stacking cap. See risks.
Practical maximum at QT3: 4.00x (ornate + scaffold + QT3) — exactly at cap.
No QT2 for exterior metal — minimum quality tier is QT3. Metal prep and coating requirements are too critical for economy-tier shortcuts.
Coat count: QT3 = 1 prime + 1 finish. QT4 = 1 prime + 2 finish. QT5 = 1 prime + 2 finish (with interstage sand).
No roll application method — metal profiles are not compatible with roller application. Brush, spray, or spray_backbrush only.
Protection tasks are NOT affected by profile complexity modifier — protection scope is driven by area/perimeter, not metal complexity.
Fixed tasks (mobilize, scaffold setup/teardown, cleanup) are not affected by any modifiers.
EA items (ornamental, misc) use TSK_METL_FINISH_ORNAMENTAL_DETAIL at 3 EA/hr. LF items use method-specific finish tasks.
Environmental modifiers (wind, sun, surface temp) are declared per exterior doctrine. High wind and hot surface BLOCK spray operations.
Metal heats faster than masonry or wood — sun exposure modifier is 1.20x (vs 1.15x for masonry) due to thermal conductivity.
risks: MODIFIER STACKING EXCEEDS 4.0x CAP: Ornate profile (2.50x) + scaffold (1.60x) + QT4 (1.15x) = 4.60x. Ornate + scaffold + QT5 (1.30x) = 5.20x. These combinations require estimator review and may need specialty pricing outside standard rate tables. Realistic worst case at QT3 is exactly 4.00x (ornate + scaffold).

Profile complexity modifier is the single largest labor variable — 2.50x on ornate work. Misclassifying moderate as standard (or ornate as moderate) creates 50-67% estimate error. Field verification of profile complexity is critical before estimating.

Rust conversion vs mechanical removal decision has dramatic cost and longevity implications. Conversion is 2-3x faster but coating life is 1-3 years vs 5-10+ years for mechanical prep. Estimator must communicate this tradeoff to client.

Aluminum 15-minute prime window creates a hard sequencing constraint that reduces effective throughput. Cannot batch-prep then batch-prime on aluminum — must section-by-section. This constraint is not captured in the base rate but is partially reflected in the rate range.
Galvanized + alkyd/oil is a catastrophic failure mode (saponification). Material system blocker rules MUST be enforced in the engine — no override allowed.
SP3 power tool prep (grinder/wire wheel) generates sparks — fire watch required on dry vegetation days. This safety constraint may limit work windows and is not captured in the production rate.

Epoxy primer pot life (4-8 hrs) creates a hard time constraint. Unused mixed epoxy must be disposed of — waste cost not captured in production rate. Mix only what can be applied within the pot life window.

Multi-substrate projects (e.g., steel railing + aluminum gutter + galvanized downspout on same house) require THREE different primer systems. Material staging and switching adds overhead not fully captured in per-task rates.
Metal overspray is harder to remove than latex overspray — DTM coatings bond aggressively to unintended surfaces. Protection adequacy is more critical than for standard painting.

QT5 zinc-rich primer requires near-white blast cleaning (SSPC-SP10) — this is a specialty service that may not be available from standard residential painting crews. May require subcontractor for blast prep.
